contributions.headingText: Deep (aggressive) angiomyxoma is an infiltrative, benign, myxoid spindle cell neoplasm that occurs in the deep soft tissue of the pelviperineal region.
2F7C & XH4V74 Neoplasms of uncertain behaviour of connective or other soft tissue & Aggressive angiomyxoma
This tumour most commonly arises in the deep soft tissues of the vulvovaginal region, perineum, and pelvis of women.

Patients typically present with a large and painless mass or ill-defined swelling. Rapid growth may occur during pregnancy. The initial clinical impression is often that of a Bartholin gland cyst or hernia. Rare tumours are pedunculated. The tumours are often much larger and extend more deeply than is initially appreciable on pelvic examination.
Deep (aggressive) angiomyxoma is typically most common in women of reproductive age, with median age in the fourth decade of life {3997139; 8646730; 6684403}.

HMGA2 encodes for a DNA architectural factor important in transcriptional regulation. Rearrangements of the HMGA2 (12q14.3) locus have been identified in approximately one third of tumours and may be intragenic or extragenic {11550285; 17654722}. Rearrangement partners include chromosomes 1, 5, 7, 8, 11, and 21, with identification of YAP1 at 11q22.1 as a novel fusion partner {11550285; 18295664; 31142482}. RT-PCR studies have confirmed the presence of aberrant HMGA2 transcript expression in deep angiomyxomas exhibiting HMGA2 locus rearrangements {11550285; 17654722; 16568309}.

The tumour is typically poorly circumscribed, with irregular extension into surrounding tissues. It can be of varying size but is often relatively large (> 10 cm), with a glistening, gelatinous to fibrogelatinous cut surface. Areas of congested blood vessels, haemorrhage, or fibrosis may be present {3997139; 8646730; 6684403; 25925211; 22288973; 18637148}.

Aggressive angiomyxoma is a uniformly paucicellular tumour composed of small oval, spindle, and stellate cells interspersed in abundant loose myxomatous stroma with delicate collagen fibrils. Mitotic activity and cytonuclear atypia are virtually absent. The stroma often contains medium-sized blood vessels, some of which have thick, muscular walls or are hyalinized. Perivascular cuffs of delicate fibrillary collagen and bundles of smooth muscle are common. Tumours lack a capsule, and soft tissue infiltration is a frequent finding, characterized by entrapment of muscle, nerve, and adipose tissue {25925211; 9023551; 18637148}.

The cells are usually positive for desmin, SMA, ER, and PR, with variable CD34 reactivity, but S100 is negative {11002763; 21804399; 25925211; 22288973; 15626915; 15735978}. HMGA2 nuclear immunoreactivity is present in most cases {20551826; 20834238}. Positivity for CDK4 but not MDM2 has been described {15735978}. The Ki-67 proliferation index is consistently low (< 1% of tumour cells).

Essential: poorly marginated; uniformly paucicellular proliferation of bland spindle cells in myxomatous stroma; medium-sized to large, often hyalinized blood vessels.

Desirable: bundles of smooth muscle cells and condensation of delicate fibrillary collagen around blood vessels.

Local recurrence occurs in as many as 30–40% of cases, sometimes many years (often decades) after the initial excision {3997139; 8646730; 6684403; 25925211}, usually if the tumour is incompletely excised initially. Adequate local excision may be difficult, because tumour extension into adjacent tissues may be greater than appreciated on clinical examination. Wide local excision (with 1 cm margins) is therefore recommended. GnRH agonist therapy has been successfully used to treat unresectable primary or recurrent tumour {16246403}.
